blockMcqs.question: What makes bit operations so cheap on a CPU?
options: They run inside a dedicated coprocessor
Each is a single hardware instruction
blockMcqs.explanation: Bitwise ops map to one native instruction the silicon does in a clock cycle.

blockMcqs.question: What does shifting an integer left by one bit do?
blockMcqs.explanation: Sliding every bit one place left raises each place value, doubling the number.

blockMcqs.question: Which identity makes XOR cancel duplicate values?
blockMcqs.explanation: Equal operands differ in no bit, so every result bit is zero.

blockMcqs.question: In two's complement, how do you compute -x?
options: Set only the top sign bit
Subtract x from the max int
blockMcqs.explanation: Inverting all bits gives ~x, and the +1 makes ~x + 1 equal -x.

blockMcqs.question: Which expression forces bit i of x to 0?
blockMcqs.explanation: ANDing with a mask that has a 0 only at position i zeroes that one bit.

blockMcqs.question: Why does (x & (x-1)) == 0 detect a power of two?
options: Powers of two are always even
It clears the only set bit, yielding 0
x-1 is always negative for powers of two
blockMcqs.explanation: A power of two has one set bit; removing it leaves zero (guard x > 0).

blockMcqs.question: An array has every value twice except one. XOR-ing all gives:
options: The sum of all distinct values
blockMcqs.explanation: Paired values cancel to 0, leaving only the element with no partner.

blockMcqs.question: Using an integer bitmask as a set, what is the union of a and b?
blockMcqs.explanation: OR keeps a bit if it is set in either operand — exactly set union.

blockMcqs.question: When is a bitmask the wrong choice for representing a set?
options: When items number in the thousands
When you need fast membership tests
When the set fits in 32 items
When you enumerate subsets of n ≤ 20
blockMcqs.explanation: A mask holds only as many items as the integer has bits; large sets overflow it.

blockMcqs.question: How do Unix file permissions like 0755 use bits?
options: rwx packed as bits, tested with AND
A sorted list of allowed actions
A hash map of user to access
blockMcqs.explanation: Nine rwx bits pack into one number; checking access is a single mask AND.

blockMcqs.question: Why must you write (x & 1) == 0 with parentheses in C?
options: & binds looser than ==, so it groups wrong
The compiler optimizes it away otherwise
blockMcqs.explanation: Without parens it parses as x & (1 == 0), testing the wrong thing.
